newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zairean rebels, day after summit talks, take town.
newsitem.headline: Zairean rebels, day after summit talks, take town.

text.p: Zairean rebels have taken the town of Kasenga, bringing them within 220 km (135 miles) of the country's second city, the copper capital Lubumbashi, expatriate and local sources said on Friday.
"It is definitely rebel troops who are in control of Kasenga," said one source with contacts in the town that lies to the south of Lake Mweru, on the river border with Zambia.

The expatriates, who declined to be identified, said the Zairean army had fled south and there were wounded people in Kasenga after clashes late on Thursday, the day the rebels agreed at a summit in Togo to talks with President Mobutu Sese Seko's government.
It was unclear whether the clashes involved fighting between the two sides or looting by Zairean troops before they fled southwards towards Lubumbashi.
Zairean military sources confirmed the town's fall, according to one well-connected Lubumbashi businessman.

Kasenga's fall surprised the sources who on Thursday cast doubt on rebel claims to be closing in on Lubumbashi, one of their next targets after the fall of the jungle city of Kisangani almost two weeks ago.
Kasenga is a small town with an airstrip and little else. It supplies Lubumbashi residents with their fish, caught in Lake Mweru.
The road from Lubumbashi to Kasenga is in poor condition, like most of Zaire's network, and what should be a two-hour journey takes eight.
